methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Proof obligation inside the masked (E-graph) model: does every rank-<=8 solution of PR1212's system (E) on P111 and on the 28 type-(4,4) P104 units equal D(2G)D^-1, so that decoders with exactly eight costly terms keep PR968's floor (63 on P111, 56 on (4,4))?
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a masked decoder can beat the floor. PR1212 answered it for exactly eight costly terms on P112/P120/type-(2,2,2,2) and listed P111 and type (4,4) as open (its PROOF.md section 10). This closes those two gaps; it does not construct a decoder.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the binding complex supplier: it rules out masked eight-costly-term decoders below PR968's floor on two more puncture families, narrowing where a cheaper masked decoder could exist (nine or more costly terms, or the 896 admissible P104 units).
stop_rule: Stop at P111 and type (4,4); the two-row classes of the admissible P104 units need a different argument and are left as a handoff.
evidence: verify.py: 26 exact checks plus 4 controls; --pr1212-dir replays PR1212's zero-exclusion DRUP proofs and orbit transport from blob-pinned files.

open_questions.question: Does rank-8 rigidity hold on the 896 admissible P104 units (PR717's P104 among them), where four classes keep only two live rows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These are the units where PR968's 7/13 ratio is attained; an off-orbit masked solution there would be the cheapest escape from the floor.
open_questions.first_step: For a two-row class, Lemma 5 leaves a one-parameter family; test whether the cross-block relations (5) with the neighbouring four-row classes fix it, on PR1212's pivot.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs a two-row variant of Lemma 5 that uses gluing equations, not only in-class relations; PR1292 gives local rigidity only.
